content:
Yesterday we saw that after Yahweh's people entered the Promised Land, they were not to forget the One who had brought them there. Every sacrifice, every offering, and every firstfruit reminded Israel that everything they possessed had first come from God. They did not offer these gifts to earn His favour or to purchase salvation. They offered them because God had already redeemed them, brought them into their inheritance, and blessed them abundantly.

The very same principle applies to us, the New Creation. We have been redeemed by the precious blood of Christ, forgiven of our sins, and made heirs of the promises of God. Therefore our lives should become continual offerings of gratitude, dedication, and obedience to the Father.

The first gift that God desires is not our money or our possessions. It is ourselves. Paul writes, "Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your reasonable service" (Romans 12:1). The New Creation belongs entirely to Christ. Our minds, our bodies, our time, our abilities, our strength, our future, and every part of our lives are to be surrendered to Him. Before God ever asks for anything from our hands, He asks for our hearts. Israel was also instructed to give the first portion of their dough to Yahweh, for He said, "Of the first of your ground meal you shall give to Yahweh a heave offering" (Numbers 15:21). This teaches us that God deserves the first place in our lives. Jesus said, "Seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness" (Matthew 6:33). Too often we offer God whatever remains after we have given our best time, energy, and attention to everything else. But the New Creation honours Yahweh by giving Him the first and the best, not what is left over.

Our worship should also continually rise before God in thanksgiving. The sacrifices in Numbers 15 were described as a pleasing aroma to Yahweh, expressing grateful worship. In the same way, the writer to the Hebrews says, "Let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name" (Hebrews 13:15). The New Creation should never cease praising God. Our lips should continually confess His goodness, proclaim His faithfulness, and testify of His wonderful works. But worship does not end with praise alone. The very next verse teaches, "Do not forget to do good and to share, for with such sacrifices God is well pleased" (Hebrews 13:16). Every act of kindness offered in Christ's name becomes an acceptable sacrifice before God. Caring for the poor, encouraging the discouraged, helping those in need, comforting the suffering, and sharing with others are all acts of worship that delight the Father's heart.

The New Creation also offers daily service to God, and everything we do should be done for His glory. Paul writes, "Whatever you do, do it heartily, as to Yahweh and not to men" (Colossians 3:23-*RNKJV*). Whether our work is public or unnoticed, great or small, every task becomes an offering when it is performed faithfully. Ordinary work becomes holy service when it is done with a willing heart. Numbers 15 also teaches an important principle concerning giving, for the offerings increased according to what Yahweh had provided.

In the same way, the New Testament teaches, "Let each one give as he purposes in his heart, not grudgingly or of necessity" (2 Corinthians 9:7), and, "According to what one has, and not according to what he does not have" (2 Corinthians 8:12). God never demands what He has not first given. He simply asks us to be faithful with whatever He has entrusted to us. Whether our resources are great or small, He delights in willing and cheerful obedience.

Our service should also be marked by joy. The New Creation is not called to serve God reluctantly, or merely out of obligation. The Psalmist says, "Serve Yahweh with gladness" (Psalm 100:2). And Paul reminds us, "God loves a cheerful giver" (2 Corinthians 9:7). The Father delights in children who serve Him joyfully, not merely because they must, but because they love Him.

And as we present ourselves to God, we must also continually lay aside our old nature. Paul exhorts believers to "put off the old man" (Ephesians 4:22), and to "put on the new man which was created according to God" (Ephesians 4:24). Pride, anger, bitterness, jealousy, selfish ambition, lust, unforgiveness, and every work of the flesh must be surrendered to God and put away. The New Creation cannot cling to the old life while seeking to live the new.

God also desires spiritual fruit from our lives. The spies once returned from Canaan carrying fruit that testified to the goodness of the land. In the same way, every believer should bear fruit that testifies that Christ is at work within.

Paul describes this fruit as "love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control" (Galatians 5:22-23). God is not seeking empty words or outward appearances. He desires lives transformed by His Spirit. And finally, everything the New Creation offers to God is accepted only through Christ. Paul writes, "Whatever you do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him" (Colossians 3:17). Christ is the One through whom every prayer, every act of worship, every sacrifice, every good work, and every expression of thanksgiving reaches the Father. Apart from Him, we have nothing to offer. Through Him, our lives become acceptable worship before God.

So Numbers 15 reminds us that God is the source of every blessing we possess. Therefore the New Creation should gladly return to Him what rightfully belongs to Him, not to earn salvation, but because we have already received His grace. Let us present our bodies as living sacrifices. Let us give Him the first and the best of our lives. Let us continually offer praise and thanksgiving.
Let us serve Him with joy. Let us do good to others. Let us bear the fruit of the Spirit. And let us surrender our whole lives to Christ. For as the apostle Paul reminds us, "You are not your own... therefore glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God's" (1 Corinthians 6:19-20).

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our God, You have redeemed us and made us heirs, so let our whole lives be an offering of thanks.

Take not only our hands and our gifts, but first of all our hearts.

Help us to give You the first and the best, and never merely what is left over.

Make our praise continual, our service joyful, and our kindness toward others a sweet offering.

Put the old man to death in us, bear Your Spirit's fruit through us, and accept us in Christ.

"Serve Yahweh with gladness. Come before him, singing with joy."

Psalm 100:2
In Christ name, through whom all our worship reaches You, we pray. Amen.
